claims.text: The proposed intervention is a post-synthesis anneal of HfZrTiTa0.53 at 0.7–0.8 of its melting temperature for 10–30 minutes followed by rapid quenching.
An anneal at 0.7–0.8 of the melting temperature constitutes a sub-transus treatment for HfZrTiTa0.53.
As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of 786 MPa.
As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 has a uniform tensile strain of 13.5% under room-temperature quasi-static loading.
The proposed anneal and quench will refine the grain structure of HfZrTiTa0.53.
The proposed treatment will create a heterogeneous grain structure with a more uniform distribution of microstructural features.
Refined and heterogeneous grains will enhance twinning and dislocation mobility during tensile deformation.
Enhanced twinning and dislocation activity will increase dynamic strain hardening and tensile ductility.
Thermomechanical processing can refine grains and improve ductility in multicomponent alloys.
Processing-mediated control of precipitate size, morphology, and distribution can produce improved strength–ductility combinations in multicomponent alloys.
The treatment will increase uniform elongation by roughly 20%, from 13.5% to approximately 16–18%.
The treated alloy will retain its yield strength and compressive strength within approximately 10% of 786 MPa and 1314 MPa, respectively.
The treatment will leave impact-triggered chemical energy release essentially unchanged.
The mechanical predictions apply at room temperature and moderately elevated temperatures under quasi-static loading near 10^-3 s^-1.

contradictions.description: A roughly 20% increase over 13.5% corresponds to about 16.2%, whereas the stated 16–18% range represents increases of about 18.5–33.3%; thus the upper part of the range is inconsistent with the stated approximately 20% target and falsification threshold.
